name: What should I do first before renovating an older home?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first before renovating an older home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with an inspection and a written scope before choosing finishes. Older houses often conceal outdated wiring, plumbing, drainage, structural changes, or moisture damage that can affect the design and budget. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate consultation, design development, construction planning, and permitting for room upgrades, additions, ADUs, garage conversions, or whole-home work. Key factors: the home’s age, prior alterations, desired layout, occupied status, and whether walls or utilities will move. Practical guidance: gather any plans, inspection reports, insurance records, and photos, then identify safety and function problems before cosmetic priorities. A coordinated design-build plan helps keep early discoveries from becoming disconnected change orders.
acceptedAnswer.description: Begin with an inspection, existing-condition review, and written scope—not demolition. Gather plans, prior permits, inspection reports, and photos, then identify outdated utilities, moisture, structural concerns, and layout goals before selecting finishes or setting a renovation budget.
